title: Coordinate compatibility for the ordered twist line
statement: Let S be a scheme, E a quasi-coherent module, and D a normalized TautologicalQuotient for its canonical symmetric relative Proj P, with projection p. Fix an ordered basis b of rank r+1, scheme comparisons eRel and theta with standard projective space, and a line isomorphism t from the pulled standard O(1) to D.line. Suppose that, for every affine open V of S and ordered coordinate i, restricting to p^{-1}(V) identifies the basis quotient p^*(iota_i followed by b) followed by D.quotient with the coordinateSection pulled through eRel followed by theta and t, using the canonical unit pullback comparisons. Then these coordinate morphisms agree globally. No geometric normalization hypotheses on eRel or theta are needed for this local-to-global implication.

proof.text: Inverse images of affine base opens cover P. The assumed equalities after restriction give equal composites into pushforward restrictions by naturality of the restriction adjunction unit. Sheaf separatedness (the proved source-library hom_ext_of_restrictAdjunction_unit) gives equality of the coordinate maps globally. The private helper proves this for arbitrary module morphisms and arbitrary p; in particular it covers empty schemes and r=0.

theorem ordered_twist_coordinate_compatibility (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules)
    [E.IsQuasicoherent] (D : ProjectiveBundleQuotientGeometry.TautologicalQuotient E)
    (r : ℕ) (b : RelativeProjectiveSpace.freeModule S r ≅ E)
    (eRel : (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProj ≅
      RelativeProjectiveSpace.scheme S r)
    (θ : RelativeProjectiveSpace.scheme S r ≅ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (r + 1)); S))
    (t : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (eRel ≪≫ θ).hom).obj
        (ProjectiveSpace.twist (ULift.{u} (Fin (r + 1))) S 1) ≅ D.line)
    (hNormalized :
      ∀ V : S.affineOpens, ∀ i : ULift.{u} (Fin (r + 1)),
      (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor
          ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ⁻¹ᵁ V.1).ι).map
        ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback
          (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom).map
        (SheafOfModules.ιFree (R := S.ringCatSheaf) i ≫ b.hom) ≫ D.quotient) =
      (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor
          ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ⁻¹ᵁ V.1).ι).map
        (((Scheme.Modules.boundaryPullbackComparison
          (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom).app
            (Scheme.Modules.unit S) ≪≫
        Scheme.Modules.pullbackObjUnitIso
          (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom).hom ≫
      ((Scheme.Modules.boundaryPullbackComparison (eRel ≪≫ θ).hom).app
          (Scheme.Modules.unit _) ≪≫
        Scheme.Modules.pullbackObjUnitIso (eRel ≪≫ θ).hom).inv ≫
      (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (eRel ≪≫ θ).hom).map
        (ProjectiveSpace.coordinateSection (ULift.{u} (Fin (r + 1))) S i) ≫ t.hom)) :
    ∀ i : ULift.{u} (Fin (r + 1)),
      (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback
          (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom).map
        (SheafOfModules.ιFree (R := S.ringCatSheaf) i ≫ b.hom) ≫ D.quotient =
      ((Scheme.Modules.boundaryPullbackComparison
          (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom).app
            (Scheme.Modules.unit S) ≪≫
        Scheme.Modules.pullbackObjUnitIso
          (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom).hom ≫
      ((Scheme.Modules.boundaryPullbackComparison (eRel ≪≫ θ).hom).app
          (Scheme.Modules.unit _) ≪≫
        Scheme.Modules.pullbackObjUnitIso (eRel ≪≫ θ).hom).inv ≫
      (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (eRel ≪≫ θ).hom).map
        (ProjectiveSpace.coordinateSection (ULift.{u} (Fin (r + 1))) S i) ≫ t.hom

statement_change.what: STATEMENT-DISPUTED (old statement): t was arbitrary. Over Spec Q with r=0, the normalized quotient is a nonzero map of line sheaves; replacing a compatible t by -t changes the right coordinate map, while every listed hypothesis remains unchanged. Add the missing affine restriction normalization, retain it in the line-existence lemma, and adapt the only caller. No proof of the old false statement is claimed. Remove the four unused scheme normalization hypotheses: they are needed for existence, not for descent of an already normalized comparison.
